detection_method: X-ray source at the centre of supernova remnant Cassiopeia A

name: NS 1987A
detection_method: Emission lines at the centre of SN 1987A ionized by a compact source (JWST spectra)
distance_method: Geometric distance of the inner ring of SN 1987A
notes: Not seen directly. Argon and sulfur lines at the centre of SN 1987A need a hot neutron star or a pulsar wind nebula to ionize them (Fransson et al. 2024). Plotted at the position of SN 1987A and its 51.4 ± 1.2 kpc distance (Panagia 2005, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0309416), far beyond the overlay's 10000-light-year radius.
outside_radius: Neutron star of SN 1987A, a remnant of the light-front topics

name: CXOU J061705.3+222127
detection_method: X-ray source with a cometary pulsar wind nebula in the Jellyfish Nebula (IC 443)
distance_method: Supernova remnant distance from the Gaia DR3 distance of its runaway former companion HD 254577
notes: Plotted at the 1701 +55/−54 pc distance of IC 443 (Dinçel et al. 2026, https://doi.org/10.1051/0004-6361/202556086). Its nebula's tail points back to the site the runaway star HD 254577 also left, and for a remnant age of 10,000–20,000 years its speed is 254–539 km/s.

name: SS 433
detection_method: Microquasar: precessing jets at 26% of the speed of light, seen in shifting emission lines
distance_method: Light-travel time across its precessing jets (5.5 ± 0.2 kpc)
notes: The plotted position represents the unresolved binary-system location. The compact object is most likely a black hole of about 5–15 M_sun (Chi et al. 2024, https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.06510), but its mass and nature are still debated, so no mass is adopted. Orbital period 13.082 days and the A7 Ib donor: Wikipedia SS 433 (Hillwig et al. 2004, https://arxiv.org/abs/astro-ph/0403634). Gaia DR3 lists a parallax of 0.118 ± 0.023 mas, too uncertain to compete with the jet distance; it is not adopted.

astrometry.astrometry_ref: Gaia DR3 proper motion via SIMBAD, https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.00211

outside_radius: SS 433, the microquasar at the centre of the Manatee Nebula (W50)

name: GRS 1915+105
detection_method: Dynamical mass of an X-ray binary
distance_method: 3D kinematic distance from its radio parallax, proper motion and the Galactic rotation curve (9.4 ± 0.6 stat ± 0.8 sys kpc)
notes: The plotted position represents the unresolved binary-system location; mass refers to the compact object. Reid & Miller-Jones 2023 revise the mass from 12.4 +2.0/−1.8 M_sun (Reid et al. 2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.2453, at 8.6 +2.0/−1.6 kpc) to 11.2 M_sun for the higher jet inclination they find; they give no uncertainty for the revised value. Orbital period 33.85 ± 0.16 days: Steeghs et al. 2013, https://arxiv.org/abs/1304.1808. Proper motion: Reid et al. 2014.

astrometry.astrometry_ref: VLBA proper motion, Reid et al. 2014, https://arxiv.org/abs/1409.2453

outside_radius: GRS 1915+105, the black hole whose jets first showed apparent faster-than-light motion in the Milky Way

name: SGR 1806-20
detection_method: Soft gamma-ray repeater; X-ray pulses
distance_method: Distance of its host star cluster from near-infrared spectroscopy of its massive stars (8.7 +1.8/−1.5 kpc)
notes: ATNF Pulsar Catalogue v2.9.0 record PSR J1808-2024: position (Israel et al. 2005), spin period and period derivative (Mereghetti et al. 2005) and proper motion (Tendulkar et al. 2012, https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8151). The characteristic age, field and spin-down power follow from this period derivative. Superseded: ATNF adopts 13 kpc (10–17 kpc) from Verbiest et al. 2012; Bibby et al. 2008 revise the cluster distance to 8.7 +1.8/−1.5 kpc.
position_source: ATNF Pulsar Catalogue v2.9.0 (Israel et al. 2005)
outside_radius: SGR 1806-20, the magnetar of the brightest flare seen from outside the Solar System until 2008

name: SGR 1900+14
detection_method: Soft gamma-ray repeater; X-ray pulses
distance_method: Kinematic distance of its host cluster of red supergiants (12.5 ± 1.7 kpc)
notes: ATNF Pulsar Catalogue v2.9.0 record PSR J1907+0919: position (Frail, Kulkarni & Bloom 1999), spin period and period derivative (Mereghetti et al. 2006) and proper motion (Tendulkar et al. 2012, https://arxiv.org/abs/1210.8151). ATNF lists no distance; it also lists a doubtful association with the remnant G42.8+0.6. The characteristic age, field and spin-down power follow from this period derivative.
position_source: ATNF Pulsar Catalogue v2.9.0 (Frail, Kulkarni & Bloom 1999)
outside_radius: SGR 1900+14, the magnetar whose 1998 giant flare ionized Earth's night-side upper atmosphere

name: Sagittarius A*
detection_method: Orbits of the S-stars (GRAVITY interferometry)
distance_method: Joint orbit fit of the stars S2, S29, S38 and S55 (GRAVITY interferometry)
notes: Supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center. Mass (4.297 ± 0.012 stat ± 0.040 sys) × 10^6 M_sun and distance 8277 ± 9 stat ± 30 sys pc from the four-star orbit fit of GRAVITY Collaboration 2022, https://arxiv.org/abs/2112.07478; the mass uncertainty combines both terms. Position: SIMBAD ICRS (Petrov et al. 2011 VLBA). The proper motion is the apparent reflex of the Sun's Galactic orbit, Reid & Brunthaler 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04386. It lies beyond the overlay's 10000-light-year radius and is kept as the black hole at the center of the Milky Way.
position_source: SIMBAD ICRS position (Petrov et al. 2011 VLBA)
outside_radius: Sagittarius A*, the supermassive black hole at the Galactic Center

astrometry.astrometry_ref: SIMBAD ICRS position (Petrov et al. 2011); apparent proper motion, Reid & Brunthaler 2020, https://arxiv.org/abs/2001.04386
